A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from AP-LDM to RepLDM. Matching equations, pseudocode, experiments, and retained results establish continuity. The complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet upsampling experiments, SAM generation benchmarks, a 16-volunteer user study, and quantitative and qualitative ablations, including Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds LAION-5B evaluations, repeated-seed results, ControlNet and SD2.1 experiments, and mechanism and efficiency analyses.

M1.justification: The default two-stage method, Equations 1–4, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged despite AP-LDM/PFSA becoming RepLDM/TFSA. Appendix D.2 adds an explicit alternative variant, TFSA-A, which pools keys and values using 2×2 pooling before attention. This limited procedural addition is tested as an ablation, not adopted as the default method.

E1.justification: v2 adds a benchmark drawn from the high-resolution subset of LAION-5B alongside the retained SAM benchmark and ImageNet pilot. It also evaluates canny- and depth-conditioned generation with ControlNet at 2048×2048 and 4096×4096, introducing materially different input conditions.

E2.justification: HiDiffusion joins the main quantitative and timing comparisons in Tables 1–2. Appendix J adds SDXL+BSRGAN as a super-resolution comparator. SDXL also joins the corresponding qualitative comparison grids in Figures 5 and 18, where v1 compared only MultiDiffusion, DemoFusion, AccDiffusion, and the proposed method.

E3.justification: New protocols include LAION evaluation using 20k reference images, 2k generated samples at 4096×4096, and KID/KIDc instead of IS/ISc. Appendix H evaluates an SD2.1 backbone with progressive scheduler [0.2, 0.2, 0.3]. Appendices E and K introduce component timing, NFE, FLOPs, and minimum-memory measurements. These extend evaluation rather than replace the retained main SAM protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds token-clustering, denoising-SSIM, Fourier, and attention-map analyses in Appendix A; decay-strategy and pooled-attention ablations in Appendix D; and guidance ablations with ControlNet, SD2.1, HiDiffusion, and DemoFusion. Robustness and component-cost analyses are also new. The original guidance-scale, delay-rate, and progressive-scheduler ablations are retained in Appendix C.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without repeated-seed uncertainty reporting. Appendix G in v2 explicitly reports three repetitions with varying random seeds and presents means and standard deviations for four methods on SAM and LAION-5B in Tables 14–15. This substantially strengthens uncertainty reporting for the central comparisons; v1 does not specify an earlier run count.

E6.justification: Shared numerical entries in Tables 1–7 are retained, but substantial new results appear in the added comparisons and Tables 8–20. For example, HiDiffusion takes 3.4 minutes versus RepLDM's 5.7 at 4096×4096 in Table 2. On the new LAION benchmark, Table 15 reports FID 34.01±0.26 for RepLDM versus 37.03±0.27 for DemoFusion at that resolution. These are added comparisons, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the token-mean deviation diagnostic mathematically in Equation 5 and derives TFSA's O((hw)^2c) computational complexity and approximate FLOPs in Appendix E. These are limited mathematical additions. The main method equations remain equivalent, and no theorem or proof framework is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains training-free high-resolution generation through attention guidance and progressive pixel-space upsampling, improving quality and efficiency. The reprogramming terminology reframes the same contribution. Although the abstract drops the explicit speedup number, the introduction and conclusion retain the 5× speedup claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive mechanism arguments about token clustering, earlier structural emergence, frequency modulation, and the residual term as a statistical anchor. It also discusses discrepancies between perceptual quality and distributional metrics, super-resolution tradeoffs, and implementation-dependent memory comparisons. The original limitations concerning text generation and extreme-resolution inference time remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the pytorch-fid implementation, discloses tiled VAE encoding/decoding and optimization choices for memory comparisons, and adds component-time and memory information. Section 4.1 changes the reported inference hardware from two 4090 GPUs to one; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. The core pseudocode and principal hyperparameters were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: The literature is updated with FouriScale, HiDiffusion, AccDiffusion v2, FreeScale, and references supporting evaluation and implementation discussions. Appendix J elaborates the relationship to super-resolution research. The existing three-category taxonomy and central novelty argument relative to prior high-resolution generation methods remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten around RepLDM, with widespread terminology changes from attentive guidance/PFSA to attention guidance/TFSA. The appendix is substantially reorganized into sections A–K with a contents list: existing comparisons and ablations move to B/C, and the algorithm moves to F. Expanded explanations, acknowledgments, and a conference checklist further change the document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous mechanism visualizations, comparison grids, ablation tables, and robustness/resource tables. Existing displays also change substantially: Figure 4 is reordered and its plot redrawn, qualitative grids gain an SDXL column and revised annotations, and several main-text figures are reduced and placed beside wrapped text. Existing appendix image grids are rearranged and condensed.

improvement.justification: v1's main evidence relies on SDXL/SAM comparisons with point estimates. v2 substantially strengthens reliability and generalization evidence through repeated-seed uncertainty reporting, LAION evaluation, additional backbones and conditioning scenarios, and targeted mechanism and resource analyses. The added comparisons reveal tradeoffs that the broad superiority language does not fully qualify: HiDiffusion is faster at larger resolutions, and SDXL+BSRGAN wins several metrics. Nevertheless, the stronger validation and more transparent comparisons provide a substantial overall quality improvement.
